decisions.summary: Layer in a Brent collar on Q3 crude exposure rather than ride the Iran-conflict volatility unhedged.
decisions.rationale: An unhedged refiner is just a leveraged bet on a war we cannot forecast. A costless collar caps catastrophic downside on margin without giving up all the upside, and it keeps trading-desk VaR inside the board limit if Brent spikes on a Strait of Hormuz event.
decisions.outcome: Collar placed on the first 45% of Q3 crude. Finance to ladder up toward 70% as the desk takes profit on the spike. Flagged for same-day review if Brent breaks $95.

decisions.summary: Pre-book West African and WTI feedstock to cut Strait-of-Hormuz-dependent sour crude from 38% toward 25% of the slate.
decisions.rationale: Single-lane dependence on Hormuz is an existential supply risk with the Iran conflict live — one closure or insurance shock strands the refinery. A more flexible crude slate costs a few cents per barrel in optimization but buys supply certainty.
decisions.outcome: Operations opened qualification on WAF and incremental WTI barrels; refinery confirmed the slate can swing. Still in progress; tied to the turnaround schedule.

decisions.summary: Require Compliance sanctions clearance on every Middle East-origin cargo before lifting — no exceptions for cheap barrels.
decisions.rationale: As OFAC tightens enforcement on Iranian crude moving through Fujairah and ship-to-ship transfers, a single tainted cargo is an existential legal and reputational risk. A clean cargo beats a cheap cargo every time.
decisions.outcome: Mandatory pre-lift sanctions screening added to the cargo workflow. Two Fujairah-loaded cargoes flagged this week for enhanced due diligence.

decisions.summary: Pass crude spikes through to pump and contract prices on a lag rather than spiking prices the day of a headline.
decisions.rationale: Spiking the pump the same day a missile hits a terminal is both a brand and a regulatory/anti-gouging risk in our retail markets. We protect margin through hedging and slate flexibility, not by gouging the pump on a war headline.
decisions.outcome: Pricing held to a lagged pass-through. Marketing to publish a transparent pass-through explainer. Flagged for review if crude stays above $95 for more than two weeks.

initiatives.title: Q3 crude-price hedging program
initiatives.summary: Ladder the hedged share of Q3 crude exposure from 45% toward 70% as the Iran conflict drives Brent volatility, keeping trading-desk VaR inside the board limit. Owned by Finance (Sam).

initiatives.title: Strait of Hormuz feedstock diversification
initiatives.summary: Cut Hormuz-dependent sour crude from 38% to under 25% of the slate by qualifying West African and incremental WTI feedstock. Tied to both supply resilience and refinery economics. Owned by Operations (Chris).

initiatives.title: Sanctions & cargo-screening compliance hardening
initiatives.summary: Pre-lift OFAC screening on every Middle East-origin cargo as enforcement on Iranian crude tightens. Two Fujairah cargoes currently under enhanced due diligence. Owned by Legal/Compliance (Taylor).

initiatives.title: Planned refinery turnaround on schedule
initiatives.summary: Complete the planned unit turnaround on schedule and incident-free despite crude-price volatility pulling at the maintenance budget. Owned by Operations (Chris) with People on safety.

initiatives.title: Retail fuels margin & pricing discipline
initiatives.summary: Hold lagged pass-through pricing through the crude spike to protect both margin and brand, with a transparent explainer on why pump prices move. Owned by Marketing (Morgan) with Commercial input.

initiatives.title: Trading-desk VaR limit review
initiatives.summary: Re-validate value-at-risk limits and stress scenarios on the crude/products desk for a Strait-of-Hormuz-closure tail case. Owned by Finance (Sam) with Commercial (Jordan).

advice_given.query_summary: How exposed are we if the Strait of Hormuz closes for a week?
advice_given.advice_summary: Materially, but survivable if we keep moving. Hormuz-dependent crude is 38% of the slate; a closure spikes Brent and freight and strands inbound VLCCs. Accelerate WAF/WTI feedstock qualification, draw on the hedge book to protect margin, and pre-position a pass-through pricing statement. Escalate any unhedged exposure above the desk limit same-day.

advice_given.query_summary: Should we hedge more of Q3 crude now or wait for a pullback?
advice_given.advice_summary: Ladder up now toward 70% rather than time the war. Use the spike to take profit on the existing collar and roll into the next tranche. An unhedged refiner through an Iran conflict is a leveraged bet on something you can't forecast — protect the margin, keep VaR inside the board limit.

scheduled_actions.intent_text: Starting from a clean baseline: research the landscape across all specialists and propose what we should be watching — add the highest-signal sources to the watchlist. Web-search the latest on the Israel–Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz shipping risk; OPEC+ output decisions and spare capacity; Brent and WTI crude price moves; OFAC and Iranian-crude sanctions enforcement; Saudi Aramco and national-oil-company supply signals; VLCC tanker rates and war-risk insurance premiums; EIA/IEA inventory and demand reports; and refiner crack spreads (Valero, Marathon, Phillips 66, PBF). Propose watchlist additions for the most decision-relevant signals, and only route something to a department head if it is genuinely urgent.
